chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
"Al-Zhahirah does not take effect when done in anger."

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Zhahirah, a specific form of divorce where a husband declares his wife to him as the back of his mother, making intercourse forbidden but not dissolving the marriage immediately.
key_terms.الْغَضَبِ: Anger, a state of emotional agitation that can affect the validity of legal acts.
key_terms.يَقَعُ: Takes effect / occurs, referring to the legal validity or enactment of the ruling.

ai.seo_question: Does anger invalidate the Zhahirah divorce declaration in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of 'Al-Zhahirah' is clarified as requiring deliberate intent, thereby excluding its validity when pronounced in a state of intense anger where composure is lost. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that legal declarations depend on the presence of mind and intentionality, distinguishing between impulsive outbursts and formal legal acts. It reflects the broader ethical emphasis on emotional stability in family law to ensure justice and clarity in marital status.
